title: Numbered list item markers
description: This latent fires on the leading marker token of an enumerated list item, specifically a digit (often followed by a period and/or bold-markdown asterisks) that begins a new entry in a numbered list, such as '5. **' or '2.'. It activates on the structural token itself rather than on the content that follows, regardless of what topic the list is about. It would not activate on prose sentences, bulleted (non-numbered) list items, or the body text following the number, since the trigger is the numeric list-marker formatting pattern rather than semantic content.

title: Numbered list item markers
description: This latent fires on the numeral token (and adjacent bold-marker asterisks) that begins an enumerated list item, such as '2.', '3.', '5. **', etc. It activates specifically at the structural position marking a new ordinal point in a numbered list or outline, regardless of the list's subject matter or the content that follows. It does not activate on the textual content of the list items themselves, on bullet points using dashes or letters instead of numbers, or on numbers used in running prose (e.g., quantities, dates, or references) that are not functioning as list enumerators.

title: Numbered list item markers
description: This latent fires on the numeral/marker token that begins an item in a numbered list, typically followed by a period and often bold formatting (e.g. '2. **', '7', '13'). It activates on the structural token itself rather than on any semantic content, appearing consistently across enumerated steps, ranked lists, or itemized headers regardless of topic. It would not activate on plain prose sentences, bullet points without numerals, or the textual content that follows the marker within the list item -- the trigger is specifically the list-numbering token/format, not the substance of what is being enumerated.

title: Empathic validation of feelings/situation
description: This latent fires on formulaic validating statements—typical of advice-giving or therapeutic register—that normalize or legitimize a person's emotional reaction or characterize the overall situation as difficult ('It's understandable that...', 'It's natural to feel...', 'That sounds like a really tough/emotional situation'). It activates most strongly on short, templated sentences that explicitly label an emotion or reaction as normal, valid, or understandable given circumstances, or that summarize a scenario as emotionally fraught. It does not activate on sentences that give concrete advice, ask clarifying questions, list options/pros-cons, or state factual/behavioral descriptions without an explicit validating or situation-characterizing frame—even if they occur in the same emotionally supportive advice-column context.

title: Numbered list item markers (small numerals)
description: This latent fires on standalone numeric tokens that serve as list or enumeration markers, most commonly small integers like 2, 3, 4, or 5 appearing at the start or end of a line, often followed by a period, as in a numbered list, outline, or step sequence. It activates strongly regardless of the surrounding topic, since the trigger is the structural role of the token as an ordinal/list marker rather than any semantic content. It does not activate on numbers used as quantities within a sentence (e.g., 'I bought 3 apples'), dates, or other numeric contexts that aren't functioning as sequential list/step markers; larger or less typical list numbers (e.g., 8, 9, 10) still trigger it but appear to do so more weakly or inconsistently, suggesting the strongest response is tied to the low, common ordinal values used in short enumerated lists.
